background_notes.fact: For a prime integer p and integers 0≤j≤λ<p, p divides none of λ!, j!, (λ−j)!, or binom(λ,j); hence binom(λ,j) is a unit in Z_(p).

grounds.reason: Any fraction with integer denominator not divisible by p belongs to R=Z_(p).

background_notes.justification: Each positive factorial factor is smaller than p and therefore coprime to p. Euclid's lemma, obtained from Bézout's identity for coprime integers, implies that a finite product of such factors is not divisible by p; 0!=1 covers empty products. The integer factorial identity λ!=binom(λ,j)j!(λ−j)! then excludes p dividing the binomial coefficient. Its reciprocal 1/binom(λ,j) belongs to R and multiplies it to 1.
